column3: “One day” and “spend the night” are supplied; the Hebrew says he went in to her.
“Let us wait” is supplied to complete the Hebrew phrase “until the morning light”.
The Hebrew repeats “midnight” and explicitly numbers the two gateposts; BSB names midnight once and says “both gateposts”.
The Hebrew leaves Samson unnamed as “he”; BSB explicitly names him.
The Hebrew explicitly says the rulers went up and gives silver without naming the shekel unit; BSB omits the upward direction and supplies “shekels”.
Close to the Hebrew.
Weakness and becoming “like one of humankind” are separate Hebrew predicates; BSB combines them as “as weak as any other man”.
The Hebrew explicitly says the rulers brought the strings up; BSB does not retain the upward direction.
The ambusher is singular, and the tow thread “smells fire”; BSB has plural men and replaces the smell image with searing. The alarm says the Philistines are “upon you”, not just “here”.
The Hebrew begins “Behold”; BSB omits it.
The binding verb is emphatically repeated, and weakness and becoming like a man are separate predicates; BSB condenses these expressions.
The Hebrew has a singular ambusher and a singular comparison thread; BSB has “men” and “threads”.
The unmarked Hebrew speech ends with weaving the seven braids into the web; BSB continues with fastening and becoming weak.
The unmarked Hebrew begins with driving in the pin; the preceding sleeping and weaving narrative is not part of that wording.
The Hebrew does not explicitly use a question verb such as “asked”; it has “said”.
The Hebrew says his “soul became short to die”; BSB replaces the image with “sick to death”.
The Hebrew says a razor has not come upon his head; BSB replaces this with his hair never having been cut.
The Hebrew has a singular collective “hand” holding the silver; BSB has plural “hands”.
Her knees are named rather than her lap. The shaving verb has a feminine subject; BSB makes her call the man to shave him.
The Hebrew says he “said”; BSB has “thought”. “Upon you” becomes “here” in the alarm.
The Hebrew actively says they bound him and then that he was grinding in the “house of prisoners”; BSB uses a passive binding and supplies the grain and compulsion.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Sacrifice” is repeated as verb and noun, and their collective hand is singular; BSB uses “offer” and plural “hands”.
Their collective hand is singular; BSB has plural “hands”.
The Hebrew states that he entertained them; BSB turns this into the purpose of summoning him.
The Hebrew calls the attendant a youth and the building a house; BSB has “servant” and “temple”.
The building is called a house; BSB has “temple”.
The Hebrew repeats its request particle and uses the vengeance root in verb and noun; BSB supplies the concrete “blow”.
The Hebrew explicitly names Samson again and calls the building a house; BSB has “he” and “temple”.
The Hebrew says “my soul” and calls the building a house; BSB has “me” and “temple”.
